subject: brain freeze
title: What If You Always Ate Ice Cream Too Fast?

scenes.text: What if you always ate ice cream too fast? The pain in your forehead doesn't start there.
Within seconds, the cold hits the roof of your mouth and chills the blood vessels just behind it.
A major artery feeding the front of your brain suddenly widens. In scans, the blood surge comes before the pain.
The signal travels along the trigeminal nerve, which also serves your face. So your brain blames your forehead.
After a few seconds to two minutes, the artery narrows again, and the pain switches off.
Brain freeze is more common in people with migraines, so scientists use ice water to study headaches.

description:
What if you always ate ice cream too fast? In a 2012 study, volunteers sipped ice water against the palate: an artery at the front of the brain widened just before the pain, then narrowed as it faded.
The pain is referred through the trigeminal nerve and usually lasts a few seconds to two minutes; it is more common in people who get migraines.
